subproblems.title: Besicovitch covering estimate for balls inside a fixed set (Simon 8.5.10, printed (4)–(5); Simon Ch. 1, 3.12)
subproblems.statement: For every N ∈ ℕ there is C ∈ ℕ (depending only on N) with the following property. Let μ, ν be measures on ℝ^N = Euclidean N (Borel σ-algebra), let A, O ⊆ ℝ^N be sets, R ∈ ℝ and t ∈ [0,∞]. Suppose every x ∈ A admits σ with 0 < σ ≤ R, B_σ(x) ⊆ O and μ(B_σ(x)) ≤ t·ν(B_σ(x)), where B_σ(x) = closedBall x σ. Then μ(A) ≤ C·t·ν(O). Here μ(A) and ν(O) are outer measures, so A and O need not be measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (μ ν : Measure (Euclidean N)) (A O : Set (Euclidean N)) (R : ℝ) (t : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ ∧ σ ≤ R ∧ closedBall x σ ⊆ O ∧ μ (closedBall x σ) ≤ t * ν (closedBall x σ)) → μ A ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞) * t * ν O
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 5 and 7 and the summation part of step 6 of the parent proof. This is the Besicovitch deduction in Simon 8.5.10 (p. 221: "Since then {B_{ρ_y}(y)}_{y∈A_1∪A_2} covers A_1 ∪ A_2 we deduce from (4), (5) and the Besicovitch Covering (§3.12 of Ch. 1) that μ(A_1 ∪ A_2) ≤ cε^{-1}(∫_{B_3(0)}‖p_S − p‖dW + ‖δW‖(B_3(0)))"). It is stated for general measures μ, ν, a general set A, a set O containing all selected balls, a radius bound R and a ratio t. The parent applies it with (μ, ν, A, O, R, t) = (μ_W, ofReal(1/ε)·‖δW‖ + ofReal(eΛ/ε)·τ, E, B°_3(0), 1, 1). Notation: B_r(x) := closedBall x r, B°_r(x) := ball x r. All quantities lie in [0,∞]. μ(A) and ν(O) are outer measures, so A and O need not be measurable.

1. The constant. Euclidean N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) is a finite-dimensional real normed space. So it has the Besicovitch covering property (Mathlib instance HasBesicovitchCovering for finite-dimensional real normed spaces, MeasureTheory/Covering/BesicovitchVectorSpace.lean). HasBesicovitchCovering.no_satelliteConfig (α := Euclidean N) gives C ∈ ℕ and τ > 1 such that there is no satellite configuration of C + 1 balls with parameter τ. Fix this C. It depends only on N.

2. The ball family. Let μ, ν, A, O, R, t satisfy the hypothesis. For every x ∈ A choose a radius σ(x) with:
 – 0 < σ(x) ≤ R;
 – B_x := B_{σ(x)}(x) ⊆ O;
 – μ(B_x) ≤ t·ν(B_x).
 The centres x ∈ A, indexed by the subtype A, with radii σ(x) ∈ (0, R] form a Besicovitch ball package (Besicovitch.BallPackage with c the coercion A → ℝ^N, r := σ, rpos from σ(x) > 0, r_bound := R and r_le from σ(x) ≤ R).

3. Besicovitch covering. Apply Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families to τ, the emptiness of satellite configurations from step 1, and this package. It gives subsets s_1, …, s_C of A (indexed by Fin C) with two properties:
 – for each k, the closed balls B_x (x ∈ s_k) are pairwise disjoint;
 – every centre lies in ⋃_k ⋃_{x∈s_k} B°_{σ(x)}(x).
 Since B°_{σ(x)}(x) ⊆ B_x (ball_subset_closedBall), A ⊆ ⋃_k ⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x.

4. Countability. Each s_k is countable by Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior, for three reasons:
 – its balls B_x are pairwise disjoint;
 – each B_x has nonempty interior: x ∈ B°_{σ(x)}(x) ⊆ interior B_x, because σ(x) > 0 (mem_ball_self, ball_subset_interior_closedBall);
 – ℝ^N is separable.

5. Summation. Each step below holds in [0,∞]:
 μ(A) ≤ μ(⋃_k ⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x)  (measure_mono, step 3)
 ≤ Σ_k μ(⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x)  (finite subadditivity, measure_iUnion_fintype_le)
 ≤ Σ_k Σ'_{x∈s_k} μ(B_x)  (countable subadditivity with step 4, measure_biUnion_le)
 ≤ Σ_k Σ'_{x∈s_k} t·ν(B_x)  (choice of σ(x), ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum)
 = Σ_k t·ν(⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x)  (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, then measure_biUnion with step 4: ν is countably additive on the pairwise disjoint closed, hence measurable, balls B_x, measurableSet_closedBall)
 ≤ Σ_k t·ν(O)  (each B_x ⊆ O, so ⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x ⊆ O; measure_mono, then monotonicity of multiplication by t)
 = C·t·ν(O)  (Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul).
 The chain also covers t = ∞, ν(O) = ∞, A = ∅ and C = 0. If C = 0, the union in step 3 is empty, so A = ∅ and the chain reads 0 ≤ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: C := the Besicovitch number of Euclidean N from HasBesicovitchCovering.no_satelliteConfig (no satellite configuration of C+1 balls with parameter τ > 1)
Choose for each x ∈ A a radius σ(x) ∈ (0,R] with B_{σ(x)}(x) ⊆ O and μ(B) ≤ t·ν(B); form the Besicovitch ball package indexed by A
Besicovitch.exist_disjoint_covering_families: C subfamilies s_k of pairwise disjoint balls whose union covers A
Each s_k is countable (disjoint closed balls with nonempty interior in the separable ℝ^N)
Sum: μ(A) ≤ Σ_k Σ_{x∈s_k} μ(B_x) ≤ Σ_k t·ν(⋃_{x∈s_k} B_x) ≤ C·t·ν(O) by subadditivity, the ratio bound, countable additivity of ν on disjoint balls and B_x ⊆ O

subproblems.title: The functional A ↦ ∫_{A×G(N,n)} g dm is a Borel measure in A (Simon 8.5.10 proof, step 2: tilt term)
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, let m be a measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n) (G(N,n) = Grassmannian N n, product σ-algebra), and let g : ℝ^N × G(N,n) → [0,∞] be an arbitrary function. Then there is a measure τ on ℝ^N such that τ(A) = ∫⁻_{A × G(N,n)} g dm (lower Lebesgue integral over A ×ˢ univ) for every measurable A ⊆ ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (m : Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)) (g : Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n → ℝ≥0∞), ∃ τ : Measure (Euclidean N), ∀ A : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet A → τ A = ∫⁻ z in A ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), g z ∂m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof. In Simon 8.5.10 (p. 221, the Besicovitch deduction from (4)), the tilt integrals ∫_{B_{ρ_y}(y)×G}‖p_S − p‖dW over disjoint balls are summed to at most ∫_{B_3(0)×G}‖p_S − p‖dW. There the functional T(A) := ∫⁻_{A ×ˢ univ} ofReal t_P(z.2) dW.measure(z) is used only through two properties: monotonicity, and countable additivity on pairwise disjoint Borel sets. This child packages both properties by showing that T agrees on Borel sets with a measure. It is stated for an arbitrary measure m on ℝ^N × G(N,n) (G(N,n) := Grassmannian N n, product σ-algebra) and an arbitrary g : ℝ^N × G(N,n) → [0,∞]. The parent applies it with m := W.measure and g(z) := ENNReal.ofReal ‖LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap z.2 − Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap P)‖.

1. Let m_g := m.withDensity g. This is a measure on ℝ^N × G(N,n) with m_g(S) = ∫⁻_S g dm for every measurable S (MeasureTheory.withDensity_apply). Mathlib's withDensity_apply needs only S to be measurable, not g.

2. Let τ := m_g.map Prod.fst, the image of m_g under the first projection Prod.fst : ℝ^N × G(N,n) → ℝ^N. This projection is measurable (measurable_fst).

3. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N be measurable.
 – By Measure.map_apply (with measurable_fst and A measurable), τ(A) = m_g(Prod.fst ⁻¹' A).
 – Prod.fst ⁻¹' A is measurable (measurable_fst hA), so step 1 gives m_g(Prod.fst ⁻¹' A) = ∫⁻_{Prod.fst ⁻¹' A} g dm.
 – Finally Prod.fst ⁻¹' A = A ×ˢ univ (Set.prod_univ).
 Hence τ(A) = ∫⁻_{A ×ˢ univ} g dm, which is the claim. ∎

Consequently T = τ on Borel sets, so T is monotone and countably additive on pairwise disjoint Borel sets, which is what step 2 of the parent proof uses. The parent evaluates τ only on closed balls B_ρ(y) and on the open ball B°_3(0). These sets are measurable, so the values of τ on non-measurable sets play no role.
proof_key_steps: m_g := m.withDensity g satisfies m_g(S) = ∫⁻_S g dm for measurable S (no measurability of g needed)
For measurable A: τ(A) = m_g(Prod.fst⁻¹'A) = m_g(A ×ˢ univ) = ∫⁻_{A ×ˢ univ} g dm (Measure.map_apply, Set.prod_univ, withDensity_apply)
